newsitem.title: USA: Clinton pledges effort on DC financial problems.
newsitem.headline: Clinton pledges effort on DC financial problems.

text.p: President Clinton said on Friday that the District of Columbia's financial problems are due, in part, to its confusing status as a quasi-city and state and pledged a "systematic effort" to address the problem.

"I am convinced that a lot of these problems have been aggravated by the 'not-quite factor' - not quite a state and not quite a city, not quite independent and not quite dependent," Clinton said at a news conference.
"There's been too much of a grey area," Clinton said. As a result, the District has found itself in a "series of pergatories" over the years, he said.
"And, very often, when functions and responsibilities are divided, they end up being nobody's responsibility, and it's easy for people to avoid the tough decisions that need to be made."
"We have to try to resolve this and I promise a more serious effort," Clinton said."
Clinton said he is "impressed" that the D.C. financial control board issued a "strategic plan" for the city on Thursday.

The hard-hitting, 46-page report warns that the District will not emerge from financial crisis unless the U.S. government assumes financing of up to $1 billion in city programs, including Medicaid, mental health care, prisons and infrastructure.
Clinton said he will respond to recommendations due out from the Office of Management and Budget on the D.C. situation and the city's financial control board.
He added, "I want to think in a larger way - what kind of systematic efforts we can make to be a constructive source in the revitalization of Washington."
